02 / WHY WE BUILT IT

Space engineering feels out of reach.

Students study equations, but rarely see how one design decision changes the outcome of a mission.

01 / COMPLEXITY

Connected systems

Propulsion, mass, fuel and thermal protection all affect each other.

02 / RISK

Failure is expensive

A small braking error or damaged engine can end a mission.

03 / PRACTICE

Few opportunities

Learners need a safe place to test, fail and try again.

05 / DECISIONS UNDER PRESSURE

When a system fails.

The simulation pauses for your decision. Every response consumes fuel, energy or structural margin.

930°C

OVERHEATING

Reduce thrust to cool the hull.

−210°C

ICING

Spend energy to warm sensors.

0%

ENGINE FAILURE

Restart or switch to a backup.

+22 KM

NAVIGATION ERROR

Correct course using extra fuel.

ADDITIONAL EVENTS: FUEL LEAK · MICROMETEORITE IMPACT · SOLAR STORM

06 / LEARNING BY CALCULATION

Landing is a math problem.

Choose braking altitude and engine burn time. The forecast changes immediately.

h ≈ v² / (2a)

h = ALTITUDE · v = APPROACH SPEED · a = DECELERATION
